sections.html:
Carol Stream sits in DuPage County, west of Chicago. The village incorporated on January 5, 1959, covers 9.44 square miles and had 39,854 residents in the 2020 census. Deeds go to the DuPage County Recorder.

Population grew from 836 in 1960 to 31,716 in 1990, peaked near 40,438 in 2000 and has been nearly flat since. Most neighbors bought within the same few decades, so comparable sales tend to be houses of similar age, and the stock is young by Chicago-area standards.

sections.h2: What Carol Stream requires before closing
sections.html:
On top of the state levy, Carol Stream collects a transfer tax of its own, and the stamp must be in hand before the closing papers go to the recorder. Finance sets the rate at $3.00 for each $1,000 of the selling price or fraction thereof.

Transfer stamp checklist
RequirementWhat to bring or do
Where stamps are issuedFinance Department at the village's main offices
FormsSigned transfer stamp declaration and the State of Illinois transfer declaration
ContractCopy of the fully executed contract showing the price
WaterFinal meter reading booked at least 2 working days before closing; final bill paid before the stamp is issued
Exempt deeds$25 administrative fee for exempt stamps

You may email the contract to Finance, as long as the file is under 25MB and is not zipped. To set the meter reading, call Water Billing at 630-871-6222. Radio readings are the norm, so staff rarely need to go inside.

sections.h2: Who pays the village tax, and can it be refunded?
sections.html:
The seller, or grantor, normally owes the village tax. When a property passes through a sheriff's sale or a tax deed, the buyer owes it instead.

The village allows a refund only when every one of four conditions is met. The seller must have lived in the house for a year within the last three, must not have rented out any part of it, must have bought and now occupy a replacement home inside the village, and must apply within one year of paying the tax. A seller who moves out of Carol Stream will not qualify.

A permit that was never closed can draw questions from a buyer's agent or the closing attorney. Community Development takes permit applications online or at its counter, and a card fee of 2.9 percent applies online and 3.5 percent in person.

  • Inspections need about 24 hours of advance notice and are scheduled at 630-871-6230 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
  • Plumbing inspections are done by a consultant on Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons, 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.
  • A re-inspection fee can apply if work fails or is not ready, and it must be paid before the next visit.

Think back to a finished basement, a deck or a water heater swap by an earlier owner, and ask Community Development if that permit was closed. An as-is cash buyer takes on the risk, while a retail buyer's lender may insist on a fix.

Illinois levies a title transfer tax of half a dollar for each $500 of declared value under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. You file the declaration through MyDec, and Carol Stream wants a copy of it when you buy the stamp.

The DuPage County Recorder files your deed, and its land records go back to 1839. Phone 630-407-5400 with questions. The office also supplies deed copies, handy for a tax appeal or an exemption.

sections.h2: Which school district is the house in?
sections.html:
School boundaries cut across village lines, so your street address decides the district. Buyers ask early, and having the answer ready spares you a question at the door.

  • Most homes: Community Consolidated School District 93, then Glenbard Township High School District 87 and Glenbard North High School.
  • Northwest corner: Elgin Area School District U46.
  • Part of the west side: Benjamin School District 25, then Community High School District 94.
  • Some southern and southeastern blocks: Community Unit School District 200 in Wheaton, or Glen Ellyn School District 41 with Glenbard North for high school.

Check the boundary with the district before you mention schools in an ad.

The Great Western Trail crosses town, and the Steve Ravanesi Trail links it to Red Hawk Park, the dog park and Glenbard North High School. The Carol Stream Park District runs 36 parks. A house within a short walk of the trail or a park is an easy item to put in a listing description. North Avenue is the main east-west corridor, and Pace Route 711 runs between Carol Stream and Wheaton.

sections.h2: Listing, selling yourself or taking a cash offer
sections.html:
An agent listing reaches the most buyers. It works best for a house in good shape when you can sit through showings, repair requests and a buyer's loan approval. If you sell on your own, you keep the agent's fee and take on the contract, disclosures and the village stamp errands yourself.

A cash sale as-is makes sense for a house with repair needs, a tenant, an estate behind it or a deadline. Expect the offer to come in under what a repaired house could fetch on the open market. Set it beside your repair estimate, your monthly carrying costs and your calendar.

Carol Stream is one of the villages where the seller handles several errands before the deed is recorded. Keep a folder with the contract, the two declarations, water receipts and permit papers, and hand a copy to your title company. If anything is missing, the Finance Department can tell you before you make the trip, and Community Development can confirm permit status over the phone. Doing those calls first keeps the stamp visit short and the closing date steady.

Once you have a signed contract, email a copy to the Finance Department. Book the final meter reading with Water Billing at least two working days before closing, and pay the final bill. Complete the village declaration and the state declaration. Pick up the stamp, pay the village tax, and bring the deed to the DuPage County Recorder.

If you plan to claim the refund, check the four conditions first. A seller who leaves the village will not qualify, so count the tax in your net before you accept a price.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Carol Stream transfer tax as the seller?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The tax generally falls on the grantor, the seller, with an exception for sheriff's sales and tax deeds, where the buyer pays. The rate is $3.00 per $1,000 of the price or fraction thereof.

faqs.q: How soon before closing should I book the water meter reading?
faqs.a: At least two working days before closing. Call the Water Billing division at 630-871-6222. The final bill, and anything else owed to the village, must be paid before the stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Carol Stream house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Most homes are in District 93 and Glenbard North, while parts of the village fall in U46, District 25, District 200 or District 41. Check the boundary with the district before you advertise the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell if a past owner skipped a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, though the issue may come up in an inspection or title review. Ask the Community Development Department at 630-871-6230 about the permit history. An as-is cash buyer may take the risk on, while a financed buyer may ask you to resolve it first.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded after the sale?
faqs.a: With the DuPage County Recorder. The state transfer declaration and the village stamp are completed before recording. Call 630-407-5400 with questions about recording.
